$comment: The bench suite. One page, one tab per bench. `status` is live | spec | planned. Rename `suite.name` freely; the page reads it from here.

suite.name: THE BENCH
suite.tagline: Can AI actually do the creative work? Five benchmarks, one page.

benches.name: PaintBench
benches.question: Can a model paint with code?
benches.summary: One painting, the most famous on Earth, recreated as pure SVG from memory. Re-run over time so you can watch models get better at a task that never changes.
measures: Recognizability: would anyone name the painting without being told
Composition, colour, craft and artistic impression
Wall-clock time to produce the SVG
Progress on the identical task, run over run
benches.judge: Claude Fable 5.1, blind to model identity and to the SVG source
benches.headline: The best model on Earth draws the Mona Lisa like a confident twelve year old.

benches.name: CutBench
benches.question: Can a model speak film grammar?
benches.summary: One brief: cut a 15 second ad. Every video benchmark scores a single clip in isolation. Films are made of cuts, and nobody measures the cut.
measures: 180 degree line: do subjects swap sides across the cut
Eyeline match and match on action across the splice
Screen direction, the 30 degree rule, state continuity
Pacing: shot length variance and where the hook lands
benches.judge: Objective gates and grammar checks first, then Fable 5.1 on the rendered cut
benches.cost: Track B, edit only, is the price of a text completion. Track A, generating every shot, is $300 to $800 a run
benches.headline: Six frontier video models. Not one can cut.

benches.name: TasteBench
benches.question: Does a model know what is good?
benches.summary: Two creative variants that ran head to head in a controlled split. Which one won, and how sure are you? Every other benchmark asks models to make things. This one asks whether they can judge.
measures: Calibration, scored by Brier, because confidence is the real question
Margin weighting: missing a blowout costs more than missing a coin flip
A human baseline: your creative directors sit the same test
benches.judge: Real campaign outcomes, not an opinion
benches.cost: Under $30 a run. The pairs are the work, not the compute
benches.headline: Fable picked the winner 64% of the time. Senior creative directors picked it 61%.

benches.name: FidelityBench
benches.question: Does the product survive the pipeline?
benches.summary: Feed a real packshot through image and video generation and measure what is left of it. Two tracks, one set of metrics: a still, and identity across four to ten seconds of video.
measures: Label text still readable, by OCR against the source
Logo geometry and brand colour delta
Hallucinated text and invented packaging detail
benches.judge: Almost entirely objective; Fable 5.1 only breaks ties
benches.headline: The number a CPG client asks for before they sign anything.

benches.name: RangeBench
benches.question: How many ideas before it starts repeating itself?
benches.summary: Hit regenerate a hundred times on one brief and cluster the results. Every practitioner has felt a model run out of ideas; nobody has published the curve.
measures: Distinct concepts before the output collapses into one mode
Diversity curve across a hundred generations
benches.judge: None. Pure embedding clustering, no model in the loop
benches.headline: Proof the suite is not just vibes at scale.
